tickets.subject: nf-300 fails image verification during scheduled upgrade
tickets.description: HarborPoint Retail opened this through the customer portal after a scheduled upgrade from Nimbus NF-300 release 5.0.8 to 5.0.9 repeatedly rolled back. The appliance downloads the image over HTTPS, but after the reboot the console stops at image verification and returns "%UPGRADE-3-IMAGE_VERIFY_FAIL". TAC reviewed the upload history and confirmed the published SHA-256 hash for the 5.0.9 image matches the file on the management host, so the image itself is intact. The failure only occurs on this 5.0.8 unit during the boot-stage verification step.
tickets.resolution: TAC identified this as KB-3104 and advised upgrading the appliance to 5.0.9, where the boot loader hashes only the unpadded payload. After the customer staged the same image and retried the upgrade, the device booted successfully into 5.0.9 and the rollback no longer occurred.

tickets.subject: image verification error after https download on nf-300
tickets.description: Pinnacle Energy emailed TAC after their Nimbus NF-300 running 5.0.8 failed two maintenance-window upgrades to 5.0.9. They reported that the image downloads successfully, but the reboot returns to the prior release and the console shows "%UPGRADE-3-IMAGE_VERIFY_FAIL". Initial checks showed the image file size and SHA-256 checksum are valid on the source server, which suggested a boot-loader verification issue rather than a corrupted download. The behavior is isolated to this 5.0.8 appliance and happens immediately after the HTTPS stage download path completes.
tickets.resolution: TAC mapped the symptoms to KB-3104 and recommended the supported resolution path: upgrade the system to 5.0.9. Once the customer performed the upgrade, the image verification step completed normally and subsequent reboot cycles retained 5.0.9.

tickets.subject: nf-300 rollback during upgrade from 5.0.8 to 5.0.9
tickets.description: A partner escalated on behalf of Cornerstone Supermarkets after a Nimbus NF-300 running 5.0.8 failed to move to 5.0.9 during a change window. The appliance accepted the HTTPS download, but the next boot entered image verification and then returned to the previous software level. The console includes "%UPGRADE-3-IMAGE_VERIFY_FAIL", while the downloaded image hash matches the published SHA-256 value. TAC confirmed the issue is tied to the boot-loader verification phase on 5.0.8 rather than to the transfer itself.
tickets.resolution: TAC identified the case as KB-3104 and directed the customer to upgrade the appliance to 5.0.9, which contains the fix for the boot-loader digest calculation. After the upgrade completed, the device remained on 5.0.9 and no further verification failures were observed.

tickets.subject: support call: nf-300 rejects valid upgrade image
tickets.description: IronGate Freight called TAC about a Nimbus NF-300 running 5.0.8 that kept reverting after an attempted upgrade to 5.0.9. The customer initially suspected a storage problem, but the appliance consistently downloads the image and then fails during the next boot with "%UPGRADE-3-IMAGE_VERIFY_FAIL". TAC asked for the image inventory and confirmed the SHA-256 hash matches the vendor-published value, which ruled out a damaged file. The issue appears only on the HTTPS stage download path and only on the 5.0.8 boot loader.
tickets.resolution: TAC matched the failure to KB-3104 and applied the documented workaround from the article: stage the image with SCP so it is written without HTTPS padding. The customer copied the image via SCP, verified it with the image status command, and the reboot completed without triggering the verification failure.

tickets.subject: nf-300 software verification failure on reboot
tickets.description: Sunset Power Authority escalated through the NOC after their Nimbus NF-300 on 5.0.8 would not complete an upgrade to 5.0.9. Operations reported that the image download finishes, but the appliance rolls back during boot and logs "%UPGRADE-3-IMAGE_VERIFY_FAIL". TAC reviewed the target image details and confirmed the checksum matches the expected SHA-256 value, so the file is valid. The behavior is consistent with a verification issue in the loader, not a transport corruption problem.
tickets.resolution: TAC identified the condition as KB-3104 and used the supported workaround: copy the image with SCP instead of HTTPS staging, then verify the image before rebooting. After the image was staged through SCP, the appliance booted cleanly and remained on the upgraded release after restart.
